title: Limit
summary: A limit states that values eventually remain arbitrarily close to a target.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared metric or topological spaces context is fixed.

content.plain: A limit states that values eventually remain arbitrarily close to a target.
content.exact: In a metric space, xₙ→L iff for every ε>0 there exists N such that n≥N implies d(xₙ,L)<ε.
content.example: The sequence 1/n converges to 0 in ℝ.
content.caveat: Limits depend on the ambient topology and on the indexing notion.
